name: Assessor - Residential Single and Multi-Family Improvement Characteristics
description: Residential single- and multi-family (fewer than 7 units) property characteristics collected and maintained by the Assessor's Office for all of Cook County, from 1999 to present. The office uses this data primarily for valuation and reporting. When working with Parcel Index Numbers (PINs) make sure to zero-pad them to 14 digits. Some datasets may lose leading zeros for PINs when downloaded. Current property class codes, their levels of assessment, and descriptions can be found on the Assessor's website (pdf) and in this class code dictionary (csv). Note that class code details can change across time. This data is improvement-level. An 'improvement' is an individual building on a parcel. Each row in a given year corresponds to a building; for example, two rows for the same parcel in one year means a parcel has two buildings. Data will be updated semi-monthly. Rowcount and characteristics for the current year are only final once the Assessor has certified the assessment roll for all townships. Depending on the time of year, some third-party and internal data will be missing for the most recent year. Assessments mailed this year represent values from last year, so this isn't an issue. By the time the Data Department models values for this year, those data will have populated. NOTE: The Assessor's Office has recently changed the way Home Improvement Exemptions (HIEs) are tracked in its data. The Home Improvement Exemption allows a homeowner to add improvements to their home that add to its value (for example, by increasing the building’s square footage, or repairing after structural flood damage) without being taxed on up to $75,000 of the added value for up to four years. For assessment modeling purposes, HIEs "freeze" a property's characteristics for a period of time, such that its assessment was based on the frozen, pre-improvement characteristics. Historically, the updated, "improved" characteristics were saved in a separate file. However, in more recent years, the improved characteristics are saved in the main characteristics file. As such, the records in this data set from before 2021 do not include HIE characteristic updates, while those from 2021 onward do include those updates. For more information on HIEs, see the Assessor's Data Department wiki. For more information on how this data is used to estimate property values, see the Assessor's residential modeling code on GitHub. Township codes can be found in the legend of this map. For more information on the sourcing of attached data and the preparation of this dataset, see the Assessor's Standard Operating Procedures for Open Data on GitHub. See additional datasets in the Assessor's Open Data Catalog.

columns.name: card_num
columns.description: Card number. Each card is an improvement/building on the parcel

columns.name: proration_key_pin
columns.description: Tieback key PIN. Prorated properties (whose value is split across multiple PINs) have a "main" or key PIN

columns.name: pin_proration_rate
columns.description: Tieback proration rate. Prorated properties (whose value is split across multiple PINs) pay taxes on the proportion of value on their PIN. In other words, assessed value is multiplied by proration rate to determine taxable assessed value

columns.name: card_proration_rate
columns.description: Card proration rate. Prorated parcels (whose value is split across multiple cards) pay taxes on the proportion of value on their card. In other words, assessed value is multiplied by proration rate to determine taxable assessed value. Cards are divisions within parcels, such as one of multiple buildings on a single parcel.

columns.name: cdu
columns.description: Condition, Desirability, and Utility code. Not well maintained.

columns.name: pin_is_multicard
columns.description: Multicard PIN. Indicates whether the parcel contains more than one building (ADU, coach house, etc.)

columns.name: pin_num_cards
columns.description: Number of cards on this parcel. Each card is an improvement/building

columns.name: pin_is_multiland
columns.description: Multiland PIN. Indicates whether parcel has more than one landline

columns.name: pin_num_landlines
columns.description: Number of landlines on a parcel. The sum of all landline square footage should be equal to the total square footage of the parcel. Each landline can correspond to a different land price/rate

columns.name: building_sqft
columns.description: Building square feet. Square footage of the building, as measured from the exterior

columns.name: land_sqft
columns.description: Land square feet. Square footage of the land (not just the building) of the property. Note that a single PIN can have multiple landlines, meaning it can be associated with more than one land price/rate

columns.name: num_rooms
columns.description: Rooms. Number of total rooms in the building (excluding baths). Not to be confused with bedrooms

columns.name: num_full_baths
columns.description: Full baths. Defined as having a bath or shower. If this value is missing, the default value is set to 1

columns.name: num_half_baths
columns.description: Half baths. Defined as bathrooms without a shower or bathtub

columns.name: num_fireplaces
columns.description: Fireplaces. Counted as the number of flues one can see from the outside of the building

columns.name: num_apartments
columns.description: Apartments. Number of apartments for class 211 and 212 properties

columns.name: garage_area_included
columns.description: Is Garage 1 physically included within the building area? If yes, the garage area is subtracted from the building square feet calculation by the field agent

columns.name: num_commercial_units
columns.description: Number of commercial units on the parcel (the vast majority are for properties with class 212)
